articles.title: JJ Watt proves to be a solid replacement for Tony Romo as CBS’s No 1 analyst
articles.summary: With the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback on leave after his arrest in July, CBS brought a dependable presence into the booth with Jim Nantz. If you were looking for insight from the CBS team broadcasting Minnesota’s 39-22 comeback win over Green Bay on Sunday afternoon, you were rewarded even…
body: Asked by his play-by-play partner, Jim Nantz, what he was focusing on with new Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray, JJ Watt told viewers that Murray was playing against his former head coach Jonathan Gannon. The now-Green Bay defensive coordinator was dismissed from the head coaching job in Arizona at the end of last season.
“Let’s see what Gannon knows about Kyler and uses against him,” Watt told the audience.

“Jim, we wondered about the chess match between Gannon and Murray,” Watt said. “Gannon decided to send everybody in. Kyler Murray with a panic throw. He just chucked it up there! And it stayed in the air forever! Easy pick for Nixon. That’s a perfect example of Jonathan Gannon using some of his knowledge to get up in the face.”

It was a picture-perfect start for Watt, who never expected to be in the No 1 chair this season. But Watt’s situation changed after the arrest of Tony Romo in July, something that prompted CBS to place Romo on leave and move Watt up from the No 2 broadcasting team.

articles.title: World’s top tennis players call truce in prize-money battle with grand slams
articles.summary: 18-month campaign comes to an end after US Open. Sinner and Sabalenka most vocal of leading players. The world’s leading tennis players have agreed a truce in their long-running battle with the grand slam tournaments over prize money, welfare and player consultation.
body: In a statement released after the men’s US Open final on Sunday the players announced they would stop their 18-month campaign of agitating against the grand slam tournaments, which culminated in a media boycott at the French Open this year, a plan first revealed in May.
A similar boycott planned for Wimbledon was called off after the All England Lawn Tennis Club made concessions.
Jannik Sinner and the US Open finalist Aryna Sabalenka were the most vocal of the players lobbying on behalf of the locker room, with Carlos Alcaraz last month withdrawing from the campaign.

The players have been calling for a greater share of the tournament revenues from the four major tournaments to be paid in prize money, a contribution from the grand slam events to player welfare and pension provision, and a formal role in decision-making through the creation of a player council.

body: Bayern had taken the lead through teenage Germany winger Lennart Karl, but Elversberg – who had won their opening two matches in their maiden top-flight campaign – levelled things up just after the hour mark thanks to a stunning curling effort from Maurice Krattenmacher.

RB Leipzig bounced back from their midweek Champions League defeat at Como by thumping strugglers Hamburg 5-0 at home. The Norway winger Antonio Nusa was the best of the bunch for the hosts, scoring one goal and setting up two more, including one for Christopher Nkunku, his first since returning to Leipzig in August.

Tidiam Gomis, Willi Orban and Rômulo also got on the scoresheet for Leipzig, who climbed to fifth in the table with the victory. Hamburg’s third heavy defeat in a row leaves the six-times German champions bottom of the table with a -12 goal difference.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev claims first US Open after four-set battle with Ben Shelton
articles.summary: No 1 seed wins 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2. American’s hopes dashed in tense final. For a passing moment at the end of a rugged third set, hope sprung anew for Ben Shelton.
body: After he had finished pumping his fist, cupping his ear to the crowd and admirably trying to initiate a drastic momentum shift, the next sequence was most revealing. Shelton opened the fourth set with a shaky game, immediately losing his serve at the start of the set. He worked hard until the end, but he was beaten by Zverev, the top seed, who closed out a 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2 victory to lift his second grand slam title of the year.

Having started his season desperately searching for his first major title, Zverev has become just the fourth man in the open era, after Jimmy Connors, Guillermo Vilas and Jannik Sinner to win his first two grand slam titles in the same campaign. He ended Shelton’s hopes of becoming the first Black American man since Arthur Ashe in 1968 and the first American man since Andy Roddick in 2003 to win the US Open.

Perhaps the most relevant detail in this rivalry is the head to head. Zverev now leads Shelton 6-0, a comfortable match-up for the German who served far better than Shelton, remained far steadier from the baseline and, as usual, nullified the effects of the left-hander’s forehand with the quality of his elite two-handed backhand.

articles.title: Intelligence & resilience key in statement win for Maresca's Man City - Murphy
articles.summary: Match of the Day pundit Danny Murphy explains how Manchester City beat Manchester United at Old Trafford despite being down to 10 men for most of the game.
body: If you go to Old Trafford in a derby, go down to 10 men in the first 25 minutes and still come away with a 1-0 victory, it tells you a lot about your players.
Sunday's result was a statement win for Manchester City 's new manager Enzo Maresca, who got his tactics spot on, but his team's performance will have showed him exactly what they are about.
I am talking about the mentality, discipline, organisation and energy you need in order to get a result when things go wrong for you like that in a game.
They were smart too, and that experience and ability not to panic goes a long way in football in situations like the one City faced following Phil Foden's early red card.

articles.title: Awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd an error, admits refereeing body
articles.summary: Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.
body: In a statement released just hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref revealed it had made contact with Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner.
The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.

Despite not touching the ball, Fernandez's movement appeared to impact the defending of Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez before Haaland's back-post finish, which by the laws of the game should have led to the goal remaining disallowed.

articles.summary: Real Madrid are up to 2nd in the La Liga standings after a 4-1 victory over Rayo Vallecano on Saturday, with goals from Kylian Mbappe (x2), Alvaro Carreras and Jude Bellingham.
body: One goal and three assists to start the season is not a bad return from Vinicius Junior, but it looks worse when compared against Real Madrid’s other big players – namely Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham. On top of this, the Real Madrid fans inside the Bernabeu have been on his back since the start of the season, and he’s yet to produce a performance that can put them in their place.

He’s tried to do it on Saturday, almost too much. There were certainly moments when he tried to force things, and it appears that the fans’ whistles are getting to him. It’s important that he takes the pressure off himself in the coming weeks, and he will need Mourinho to help him with that.

Diomande has had to be patient since joining Real Madrid in the summer, but he finally made his first start against Rayo – and it was a chance that he took. The Ivorian winger was mightily impressive in the first half, both in defence and attack, and this will have greatly pleased Mourinho.

articles.title: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat
articles.summary: Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.
body: Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions.
However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.

The VSC only lasted two minutes, so Norris was unable to pit on the next lap as the VSC period ended just before he reached the pit entry. He pitted under green flag conditions and dropped to fifth on the track, before recovering to third by the end of the race.

"I was just unlucky. I was the only one on the whole grid to not get a pit stop and lost 20 seconds. This was out of there [the team's] control, my control. It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," Norris told Sky Sports F1.
